messages.subject: BLUP interpretation
parts:
Hi Folks,
We have a dataset with known mothers and some (most) known fathers. In the PBV.full results we got the number of  BLUPs which sums up to the number of mothers, fathers and all individuals. How to interpret the values we got? We suppose that BV for mothers go first, then for fathers and then for the individual trees in the test. Is that right?

Jan Kowalczyk
Daniel Chmura

messages.author: 37c4b6bc71d5d203
messages.subject: Re: [breedR] BLUP interpretation
parts:
Dear Jan and Daniel,

The order of the result depends on the original coding scheme, and whether there has been need of recodification or not.

Here is a toy example with 15 individuals in total (only 5 observed), with random codes where you recover the BVs in the original codification. It is completely general and works under any circumstances.

set.seed(123); n.ped <- 5
ped.nightmare <- matrix(sample(30, n.ped*3), n.ped, 3,
                        dimnames = list(NULL, c('self', 'sire', 'dam')))

## Obviously, the pedigree is recoded
ped <- build_pedigree(1:3, data = ped.nightmare)
#> Warning in build_pedigree(1:3, data = ped.nightmare): The pedigree has been
#> recoded. Check attr(ped, 'map').

## Simulated data
(dat <- data.frame(
  ped.nightmare,
  y = rnorm(n.ped)
))
#>   self sire dam          y
#> 1    9    2  20  1.2805549
#> 2   23   13  30 -1.7272706
#> 3   12   21  22  1.6901844
#> 4   24   27  29  0.5038124
#> 5   25   10  26  2.5283366

## Fitted model
res <- remlf90(
  fixed = y ~ 1,
  genetic = list(
    model    = 'add_animal',
    pedigree = ped,
    id       = 'self'
  ),
  data = dat
)
#> No specification of initial variances.
#>      Using default value of 1 for all variance components.
#>      See ?breedR.getOption.

## BV in internal codes (sorted, consecutive, from 1 to 15)
BV <- ranef(res)$genetic

## Get the BLUPs for all 15 individuals in the original codes
## use the "map" attribute of the recoded pedigree
data.frame(
  BV = BV[attr(ped, "map")]
)[!is.na(attr(ped, "map")),, drop = FALSE]
#>             BV
#> 2   0.10618394
#> 9   0.21236787
#> 10  0.41761928
#> 12  0.41684771
#> 13 -0.64454290
#> 20  0.10618394
#> 21  0.20842385
#> 22  0.20842385
#> 23 -1.28908580
#> 24 -0.17536833
#> 25  0.83523855
#> 26  0.41761928
#> 27 -0.08768416
#> 29 -0.08768416
#> 30 -0.64454290


Hope it helps!
    ƒacu.-
